concepts.title: Electrostatic Potential from Work per Unit Charge
concepts.definition: The potential at a point records how much work each coulomb of positive charge costs an outside agent to carry in from an infinite distance.
concepts.key_idea: Only potential differences carry physical meaning; the zero of potential is a free choice, conventionally set at infinity.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph102.txt sections 2.1-2.2 (potential energy, potential definition, Eq. 2.4)
question_patterns: a test charge of 5 nanocoulomb costs 2 times 10 to the minus 6 joule to bring in; compute the potential at that point
a charge of 2 nanocoulomb needs 8 times 10 to the minus 5 joule of work to reach point P from infinity; find the potential there
how much work moves a 2 microcoulomb charge across a potential difference of 100 volt
find the potential difference if 0.05 joule shifts a 2 microcoulomb charge between two terminals
why do only potential differences matter physically while the absolute potential is arbitrary up to a constant
0.05 joule shifts a 2 microcoulomb charge between two terminals; get the potential difference and say why only differences matter

solution_steps.action: split the work by the charge moved
solution_steps.explain: potential difference equals work done per unit charge, so divide work by the test charge

concepts.title: Potential Due to a Point Charge
concepts.definition: A point charge Q sets up around itself a potential equal to k Q over r, dropping as one over distance and carrying the sign of the source charge.
concepts.key_idea: Potential falls as 1/r while field falls as 1/r squared, so potential is the gentler falloff of the two.
question_patterns: calculate the potential at 9 cm from a 4 times 10 to the minus 7 coulomb charge
find the potential at distance r from a point charge Q placed in vacuum
what is the electric potential 30 cm away from a 10 nanocoulomb point charge
evaluate the potential near a point source charge with the one-over-r rule
determine V at 18 cm from the centre of a small charged sphere treated as a point

solution_steps.explain: the point-charge potential is k Q over r with k = 9e9 in SI units

solution_steps.action: multiply by charge and divide by distance
solution_steps.explain: scaling the constant by the source charge and the reciprocal distance gives the potential

concepts.title: Potential Due to a Dipole at a Far Point
concepts.definition: Far from a dipole the potential equals k p cos theta over r squared, so it falls as one over r squared, flips sign between the two axial directions, and vanishes over the whole equatorial plane.
concepts.key_idea: Dipole potential dies one power of r faster than a point-charge potential and depends on the angle to the moment, not on r alone.
question_patterns: calculate the far potential of a dipole with charges 2 nanocoulomb separated by 1 cm at a point 30 cm away at 60 degrees to its moment
find the potential at a distant point on the axis of a short dipole with charge q and separation 2a
what potential does a dipole of moment p give at distance r and angle theta
show that the potential in the equatorial plane of a dipole is zero and verify it numerically with cos 90 degrees
how does the dipole potential fall with distance compared with the potential of a single charge

solution_steps.explain: the moment is charge times full separation, the product the far field actually responds to

solution_steps.action: scale by angle and inverse square
solution_steps.explain: multiply k by the moment and cos(theta), then divide by the squared distance

concepts.title: Potential of a Charge System by Superposition
concepts.definition: Potential obeys superposition as an algebraic sum: every charge contributes k q over its own distance, signs included, with no interference between terms.
concepts.key_idea: Because potential is a scalar, adding contributions needs no vector geometry, only careful signs and the right distances.
question_patterns: charges of 4 and -3 microcoulomb sit 20 cm apart; find the potential at the midpoint of the line joining them
two charges of 3 times 10 to the minus 8 and -2 times 10 to the minus 8 coulomb lie 15 cm apart; evaluate the potential at a point 10 cm from each
add the potentials from two point charges placed at given distances from a point
what potential does a pair of charges produce at a nearby point P
compute V at a point using the algebraic sum rule for a two-charge system

solution_steps.explain: apply the point-charge rule to charge1 with its own distance to the field point
repeat for charge2 at its own distance, keeping its sign
potentials superpose as plain signed numbers, so the total is their arithmetic sum

concepts.title: Equipotential Surfaces and the Field-Potential Link
concepts.definition: An equipotential surface joins points sharing one potential value; the field meets it at right angles and points down the steepest potential slope.
concepts.key_idea: No work is needed to slide a charge along an equipotential, which is exactly why the field can have no component along it.
question_patterns: why is the electric field always normal to an equipotential surface
describe the equipotential surfaces drawn around a single point charge
what shape do the equipotential surfaces take inside a uniform field along the x axis
how is the field strength related to the rate at which potential drops with distance
can two different equipotential surfaces ever touch or cross each other
in which direction does the electric field point relative to the steepest decrease of potential
the field runs down the steepest potential slope; state its size as the potential change per unit normal distance

solution_steps.action: apply the no-work condition on the surface
solution_steps.explain: moving a test charge between points of equal potential needs zero work, so the field cannot have a tangential part
the field must therefore cross every equipotential at right angles

solution_steps.action: read the field from the potential gradient
solution_steps.explain: the magnitude equals the potential change per unit normal distance, directed down the slope

concepts.title: Potential Energy of Two Charges
concepts.definition: Assembling two charges at a fixed separation stores work as energy k q1 q2 over r12, positive for like charges and negative for unlike ones.
concepts.key_idea: The energy belongs to the configuration, not to the assembly route, because electrostatic work is path-independent.
question_patterns: calculate the potential energy of two charges 7 and -2 microcoulomb kept 18 cm apart
how much work does it take to assemble two like charges at a stated separation
find the energy stored in a pair of opposite charges a given distance apart
work needed to pull two charges of known values and separation infinitely far apart
determine U for charges q1 and q2 whose gap is r12 in vacuum

solution_steps.explain: the pair energy uses the same constant as the force law
multiply k by both charges and divide by their separation to get the stored energy

concepts.title: Potential Energy of a Dipole in a Field
concepts.definition: A dipole of moment p tilted at angle theta inside a uniform field carries potential energy minus pE cos theta, least when aligned with the field.
concepts.key_idea: Alignment is the low-energy state; turning the dipole away from the field costs work that comes back as torque when released.
question_patterns: find the potential energy of a dipole of moment 4 times 10 to the minus 9 coulomb metre held at 30 degrees inside a 5 times 10 to the 4 field
calculate the energy of a dipole aligned at angle theta to a uniform field
at what orientation is the dipole energy minimum and what is its value there
compute minus p E cos theta with numbers for a molecule in a strong field
a molecular dipole of moment 1 times 10 to the minus 29 sits at 60 degrees inside a 1 times 10 to the 6 volt per metre field; find its energy

solution_steps.action: project the field on the moment
solution_steps.explain: only the field component along the moment counts, so multiply pE by cos(theta) and attach the minus sign

concepts.title: Electrostatic Properties of Conductors
concepts.definition: In the static state a conductor shows five hallmark behaviours: zero interior field, a surface field strictly perpendicular to the face, excess charge living only on the surface, one constant potential everywhere within and on the body, and complete shielding of an empty cavity.
concepts.key_idea: Free electrons rearrange until the interior field cancels; that single fact generates all five conductor rules including shielding.
question_patterns: free electrons inside a metal keep drifting until which condition on the interior field is reached
where does any excess charge on a charged conductor reside in the static case
why must the field just outside a charged conductor point along the perpendicular there
a cavity in a conductor stays free of outside electrical influence; name this effect and give the outside surface field sigma over eps0
is the potential the same at every point of a charged conductor and on its surface
five hallmark static behaviours of a conductor; list them and connect each to zero interior field

solution_steps.explain: any residual field would drive the free electrons until it cancels, defining the static state
a Gauss pillbox inside the body encloses zero flux, hence zero interior net charge

solution_steps.action: set the surface field and shielding
solution_steps.explain: the surface field is sigma over eps0 along the outward normal, and an empty cavity stays field-free whatever happens outside

concepts.title: Dielectrics and Polarisation
concepts.definition: A dielectric is an insulator whose molecules stretch or swing round inside a field, building bound surface charges that partially cancel the applied field within the slab.
concepts.key_idea: Polar molecules already carry a moment while non-polar ones gain an induced one; both end up polarised with the field reduced, not erased as in a conductor.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph102.txt section 2.10 (Eq. 2.37, polar and non-polar molecules)
question_patterns: which dielectric molecules carry a permanent moment and which only gain an induced one inside a field
what happens inside a dielectric slab placed in an external field
define polarisation and electric susceptibility for a dielectric medium
why does sliding a dielectric between capacitor plates weaken the field there
what are the induced surface charges on a polarised slab and why are they called bound charge

solution_steps.explain: non-polar molecules have coinciding charge centres, polar ones keep separated centres with a permanent moment
the field stretches non-polar molecules or lines up polar ones, giving a net moment per unit volume

solution_steps.action: account for the induced surface charge
solution_steps.explain: unaligned dipole ends pile up on the faces normal to the field, and their field opposes but does not fully cancel the applied one

concepts.title: Capacitance and Plate Charge
concepts.definition: Capacitance is the charge a capacitor stores per volt across its plates, fixed by geometry and any filling material; the stored charge follows by multiplying it by the applied voltage.
concepts.key_idea: A farad is enormous, so practical capacitors sit in the micro, nano and picofarad range; C never depends on Q or V themselves.
question_patterns: how much charge collects on each plate of a 12 picofarad capacitor wired to a 50 volt battery
a 100 volt supply charges a 900 picofarad capacitor; find the plate charge
calculate the charge stored when a capacitor of capacitance C is raised to potential difference V
a capacitor rated 8 picofarad is wired to 100 volt; how much charge does each plate carry
compute the charge on a capacitor from its capacitance and the applied voltage
define capacitance and give its SI unit

solution_steps.explain: the defining ratio Q over V rearranges to give the stored charge directly

concepts.title: Parallel Plate Capacitor Capacitance
concepts.definition: Two wide plates a narrow gap apart hold capacitance eps0 A over d, set purely by plate area, separation and the filling medium.
concepts.key_idea: The field lives only in the gap and equals sigma over eps0, which is what turns the geometry directly into capacitance.
question_patterns: find the capacitance of an air-filled parallel plate capacitor with plates of 6 times 10 to the minus 3 metre squared held 3 mm apart
calculate C for two parallel plates of area A separated by distance d in vacuum
what capacitance does a plate pair of given area and gap have in air
compute the geometric capacitance of a parallel plate arrangement from its dimensions
plates of 1 metre by 1 metre spaced 1 mm apart; estimate their capacitance in farad

solution_steps.action: scale eps0 by area over gap
solution_steps.explain: insert eps0 = 8.85e-12, multiply by the plate area and divide by the separation

concepts.title: Dielectric Filling and Capacitance Gain
concepts.definition: Filling the gap with a dielectric multiplies the vacuum capacitance by the dielectric constant K, because polarisation shrinks the interior field and with it the plate voltage.
concepts.key_idea: K above 1 is the capacitance growth factor; permittivity of the medium is eps0 K, and a thinner gap scales C up in the same ratio.
question_patterns: an air capacitor of 8 picofarad has its gap halved and the space filled with material of constant 6; find the new capacitance
what happens to the capacitance when a dielectric slab of constant K fully fills the gap
calculate the new capacitance after inserting a sheet with dielectric constant 6 between the plates
express the filled capacitance through the vacuum value and K and evaluate it with numbers
a mica sheet of constant 6 as thick as the gap slides in; get the resulting capacitance

solution_steps.explain: capacitance varies as one over the gap, so closing the gap multiplies C by old gap over new gap
the filled capacitance is K times the vacuum value times the geometry factor

concepts.title: Capacitors in Series
concepts.definition: Chaining capacitors end to end puts one shared charge on every unit while voltages add, so the reciprocals of the capacitances add and the equivalent comes out smaller than the smallest member.
concepts.key_idea: Series shares charge but splits voltage; the reciprocal rule converts the added drops into one equivalent capacitance.
question_patterns: three 9 picofarad capacitors joined in series; find the combination capacitance
two capacitors C1 and C2 connected in series; obtain the equivalent capacitance
capacitors of 2, 3 and 4 picofarad chained in series; what single capacitance can replace them
find the total capacitance when several capacitors are wired one after another
compute the equivalent of a series chain from the individual capacitances with given values

solution_steps.explain: equal charge and added voltage drops make the reciprocals of the capacitances add
the equivalent capacitance is the reciprocal of the summed reciprocals

concepts.title: Capacitors in Parallel
concepts.definition: Wiring capacitors side by side puts the same voltage on every unit while their charges add, so the capacitances add straight to one larger equivalent.
concepts.key_idea: Parallel shares voltage but pools charge, giving an equivalent at least as large as the biggest branch.
question_patterns: capacitors of 2, 3 and 4 picofarad wired in parallel; find the total capacitance
what is the combined capacitance of a parallel bank of capacitors
three capacitors in parallel across a 100 volt supply; find the equivalent capacitance value
add up parallel capacitances to get one replacement capacitor
two capacitors of 6 and 3 picofarad in parallel; compute the equivalent

solution_steps.explain: common voltage means charges C1V, C2V and so on add, so the capacitances simply add

concepts.title: Energy Stored in a Capacitor
concepts.definition: Charging a capacitor pumps energy one-half C V squared into the field between its plates, recoverable in full when the capacitor discharges.
concepts.key_idea: The same energy reads Q squared over 2C or one-half QV; the field view gives an energy density of one-half eps0 E squared per unit volume.
question_patterns: how much energy does a 12 picofarad capacitor charged to 50 volt store
calculate the electrostatic energy held by a 600 picofarad capacitor at 200 volt
find the energy stored in a capacitor from its capacitance and charging voltage
a 900 picofarad capacitor is charged by a 100 volt battery; compute the stored energy
the stored energy of a charged capacitor reads one-half Q V; evaluate it for a 900 picofarad unit at 100 volt

solution_steps.action: apply the one-half C V squared rule
solution_steps.explain: charging work integrates Q dQ over C, ending at half the product of capacitance and voltage squared
